questions.q: What real Northbridge workflow does the capstone project, launch_store.py, automate?
options: Processing customer returns
Compiling the company's annual financial report
Rotating employee work schedules
The repetitive checklist run by hand every time Northbridge opens a new store
questions.explain: The capstone scripts the new-store setup checklist: config file, admin user setup, inventory baseline pull, and an ops team notification -- a real task currently done by hand each time a store opens.

questions.q: Why does the kickoff lesson emphasize building one workflow completely rather than several workflows partway?
options: Multiple workflows would require a different programming language
A script that reliably completes one real workflow end to end demonstrates the skills more convincingly than a sprawling tool that does more but fails partway through
Because argparse can only handle one script per project
Northbridge only has one server available for testing
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly argues that one complete, working workflow is more valuable to demonstrate than several half-finished ones -- completeness over the appearance of scope.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's pattern does the admin-account step in launch_store.py reuse?
options: Lesson 3, Text Processing Pipelines
Lesson 6, Working With Files & the OS
Lesson 10, JSON in Python
Lesson 18, Automating User & Server Setup, specifically its idempotent setup routine
questions.explain: The kickoff explicitly maps the admin-account step onto lesson 18's idempotent user-setup pattern, so the account creation can be safely rerun without duplicating work.

questions.q: According to the "done" checklist, where should the inventory API's authentication token come from?
options: Hardcoded directly into launch_store.py
A comment at the top of the file
An environment variable, never hardcoded in the script
The store's config filename
questions.explain: The checklist calls for no hardcoded secrets -- the API token is read from an environment variable, following the same secrets-handling rule established earlier in the course.

questions.q: How many Slack alerts does a single run of launch_store.py send, according to the plan?
options: None -- Slack alerts are only used in lesson 21
Exactly one at the end of the run, reporting either success or exactly what failed
One per minute until someone acknowledges it
One for every individual step in the workflow
questions.explain: The done checklist specifies a single summary alert at the end of the run, rather than one alert per step, so ops gets one clear signal about the outcome.
